oil.summary: Crude markets are caught in a paradox: approximately 14 Iranian Hormuz attacks in November alone, a Trump-Putin diesel deal unravelling, and Russian missiles striking Kyiv have done little to sustain prices. Brent shed another 2.3% today to $89.87 and is now off more than 20% on the month, with WTI holding slightly firmer at $83.62 (+0.49%). The bearish read is structural: recovering Gulf oil flows are absorbing the geopolitical risk premium, Iran's own crude is reportedly still moving through the Strait, and China's October Gulf imports surged 42.4% month-on-month—suggesting aggressive restocking rather than shortage. Japan's plan to replenish up to 8 million barrels of Saudi crude drawn during the Hormuz crisis adds to the demand-side narrative. CME options now price a 77% probability of an OPEC cut at the May 2027 meeting, underscoring market concern about the demand trajectory.
drivers: Gulf oil flows recovering despite ~14 Iranian Hormuz attacks in November, capping the geopolitical risk premium and pushing Brent -20% on the month
Trump-Ukraine energy truce collapse and stalled Russia diesel deal inject political uncertainty without translating into supply disruption priced by the market
OPEC cut probability at 77% for May meeting signals traders expect production discipline will be needed to stabilise prices at current levels

gas.summary: Henry Hub surged 16% today to $3.791/MMBtu, extending a blistering month that has seen prices rise nearly 36%. The Iran war's status as the largest oil and gas disruption on record is feeding through to global LNG pricing, tightening supply available to both Asian and European buyers. Europe entered winter already stressed: storage has drained 11% of summer injections in under a month from a low starting point, keeping TTF elevated at 88.7 €/MWh (+5% today) despite a slight weekly pullback. Norway's gas sales jumped nearly 20% in October, running 5.6% above year-ago levels, but incremental Norwegian supply alone appears insufficient to offset the regional deficit. India's LPG consumption hit an eight-month high in October as supply gradually recovered post-Hormuz disruption. A rising U.S. rig count provides some medium-term relief signal but offers no near-term balance.
drivers: Henry Hub +16% on the day, +36% on the month, driven by global LNG tightness stemming from the Iran-war supply disruption
European storage drawdowns have already consumed 11% of summer injections with winter just starting, keeping TTF structurally bid
Norway export surge (+20% in October) and rising U.S. rig count are partial offsets but insufficient to relieve near-term tightness

power.summary: EU carbon edged up 2.8% to $78.40/EUA today, partially recovering from a sharp 9% weekly loss, as surging TTF gas prices (+5% on the day) lift the marginal cost of gas-fired generation and feed into allowance demand. The broader macro backdrop is shaped by a high-profile Trump-Xi-Putin summit on the APEC sidelines that delivered what sources describe as big promises but few breakthroughs, leaving energy market structural risks unresolved. On the demand side, a headline on U.S. data centre capacity highlights that Democratic governors will oversee states hosting 77% of the 300 GW of data centre build announced for 2027-2030, flagging a new political variable for power load growth. Houthi activity continued, with a Saudi-led coalition targeting weapons smuggling at Hodeidah port overnight. The power and carbon space has limited dedicated price-driver news today beyond the gas and geopolitical read-across.
drivers: TTF +5% on the day lifts gas generation costs and supports EUA demand, partially reversing the week's 9% EUA selloff
Trump-Xi-Putin summit produced no concrete energy or sanctions breakthroughs, leaving supply-disruption risk unresolved for carbon-intensive generation
U.S. data centre build concentrated in Democrat-governed states introduces a new political dimension to future power load and clean-energy procurement
